quality.rejected_note: Rejection belongs to the research contract (schema, every quote found); an analysis that reached this rubric passed it, and this rubric rejects nothing.

findings.rule: A number in a statement does not appear anywhere in the source text.

checks.source_too_short: The source has fewer than 30 words or no words beyond its headline, so it may be a headline or a feed excerpt rather than a publication.
checks.source_may_be_cut: The source ends with an ellipsis or a 'read more' marker, or without closing punctuation, so it may be cut off.
checks.number_not_in_source: A number in a statement does not appear anywhere in the source text.
checks.number_not_in_quotes: A number in a statement appears in the source, but not in that statement's own quotes.
checks.unit_differs: A number in a statement carries another unit than the same number in its quotes (percent against percentage points, millions against billions).
checks.level_change_differs: A figure a statement gives as the size of a change ('by', or after a rise or fall word) is a level reached ('to') where its quote's sentence states it, or the reverse.
checks.period_not_in_source: A month, quarter, year or date in a statement does not appear in the source text.
checks.period_not_in_quotes: A month, quarter, year or date in a statement is neither in that statement's own quotes nor the one their sentence gives a figure they quote.
checks.forecast_unattributed: A statement with basis forecast names no expectation or attribution word.
checks.assessment_unattributed: A statement with basis assessment names no attribution word.
checks.basis_mismatch: A statement with basis data or action uses future or expectation wording.
checks.beyond_quotes: Several content words of a statement are not in its quotes or the source sentences they come from, so it may say more than they do.
checks.direction_differs: A statement says something rose, fell or was unchanged (or did not) where its quotes state another direction.
checks.negation_differs: A statement negates a word that its quotes and their sentences state with no negation, or states without a negation a word that they negate.
checks.speaker_not_in_source: A statement attributes its content to a speaker the source and headline do not name.
checks.speaker_differs: A statement attributes its content to a speaker that the sentence its quotes come from does not name, although that sentence names its own speaker (the headline counts for the publisher).
checks.interpretation_number_not_in_source: A number in the interpretation does not appear in the source text.
checks.absence_contradicted: A missing-information item says something is absent, but every key term of it appears together in one paragraph of the source.
checks.no_unknowns: The analysis lists no missing information and no tests.

human_review: Whether each statement is an accurate paraphrase of its quotes, beyond the words and figures checked here.
Whether the interpretation follows from the statements it names.
Whether the assumptions, competing explanations and tests are apt and complete.
Whether the analysis left out something the source establishes that matters.
quality.statement: Lexical checks of words, figures, units, periods and attribution. A flag asks a person to look; no flag is not a confirmation that the analysis is correct.
